candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7: prioritize care, utilize resources, collaborate, organize workload, and participate in quality-improvement activities.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — safe staffing, workload and resource planning
candidate.educational_objective: Explain why direct-care nurses belong on staffing committees: their frontline knowledge helps align staffing plans with patient acuity, care needs, workload, and staff skills.

options.A: To incorporate frontline knowledge of patient acuity, care needs, workload, and staff skills into unit staffing plans.
options.B: To exclude direct-care nurses from staffing decisions so planning remains entirely administrative.
options.C: To use one fixed staffing number for every shift without considering acuity, workload, or skill mix.
options.D: To transfer staffing decisions to personnel with no direct knowledge of unit-level patient-care demands.

candidate.rationale: ANA describes staffing committees as nurse-led groups that develop unit-level staffing plans based on patient population acuity and needs together with staff skills and experience, and supports substantial direct-care nurse representation. Direct-care nurses contribute frontline knowledge of actual patient-care demands and staffing conditions. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Direct-care nurse representation brings frontline knowledge of patient acuity, care needs, workload, and staff skills into staffing-plan development.
candidate.source_document_title: Advocating for Safe Staffing in Nursing
